Stratum-specific ORs and omnibus LRT for a fitted interaction term

Source: R/interaction_table.R
mysterycall_interaction_table.Rd

Given a mysterycall_logistic_model() object whose $model already contains an interaction term (e.g. insurance:specialty), this function extracts the interaction rows from $or_table, performs an omnibus likelihood-ratio test (LRT) by refitting the model without the interaction, and returns a tidy list suitable for manuscript reporting.

Usage

mysterycall_interaction_table(fit, var1, var2, conf_level = 0.95, digits = 2L)

Arguments

fit

A mysterycall_logistic_model object returned by mysterycall_logistic_model(). The $model element must have been fitted with the interaction term var1:var2 (or var1*var2) in the fixed-effects formula; otherwise no rows will be found and the function stops with an informative message.

var1

Character scalar. First variable in the interaction (e.g. "insurance").

var2

Character scalar. Second variable in the interaction (e.g. "specialty").

conf_level

Numeric scalar strictly between 0 and 1. Confidence level used to label CIs in the printed output. Default 0.95.

digits

Non-negative integer scalar. Decimal places for ORs and the LRT p-value in formatted output. Default 2L.

Value

A list of class mysterycall_interaction_table containing:

interaction_ors

tibble::tibble() with one row per interaction contrast and columns term, or, ci_lower, ci_upper, p_value_fmt. ORs and CIs are rounded to digits places.

lrt_p

Numeric. Omnibus LRT p-value (NA if the refit failed).

lrt_p_fmt

Character. Formatted LRT p-value (e.g. "0.003" or "< 0.001").

sentence

Character. Ready-to-paste manuscript footnote, e.g. "The interaction between insurance and specialty was statistically significant (LRT p=0.003)."

var1

Character. Echo of the var1 argument.

var2

Character. Echo of the var2 argument.

digits

Integer. Echo of the digits argument.

conf_level

Numeric. Echo of the conf_level argument.

Details

The LRT refits the model with update() dropping only the var1:var2 term, then calls stats::anova() on the two models. If the refit fails for any reason (e.g. convergence, missing lme4, or a NULL $model in a fake object) the LRT p-value is set to NA with a warning rather than stopping.

Manuscript use

Paste result$sentence directly into a Table footnote. Use result$interaction_ors as a supplemental panel or within-table stratum block.

Examples

# Fake a mysterycall_logistic_model object -- no lme4 required.
# The LRT refit will be caught by tryCatch (model = NULL) and lrt_p = NA.
fake_or_table <- data.frame(
  term        = c("(Intercept)",
                  "insuranceMedicaid",
                  "specialtyGYN",
                  "insuranceMedicaid:specialtyGYN",
                  "insuranceMedicaid:specialtyOB"),
  estimate    = c( 0.80, -0.20,  0.15, -0.45,  0.31),
  se          = c( 0.18,  0.14,  0.12,  0.21,  0.19),
  z_value     = c( 4.44, -1.43,  1.25, -2.14,  1.63),
  p_value     = c( 0.001,  0.153,  0.211,  0.032,  0.103),
  p_value_fmt = c("< 0.001", "0.153", "0.211", "0.032", "0.103"),
  or          = c( 2.23,  0.82,  1.16,  0.64,  1.36),
  ci_lower    = c( 1.56,  0.62,  0.92,  0.42,  0.94),
  ci_upper    = c( 3.19,  1.08,  1.46,  0.97,  1.97),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
fake_fit <- structure(
  list(
    model      = NULL,
    or_table   = fake_or_table,
    n          = 200L,
    n_clusters = 40L,
    formula    = stats::as.formula(
                   "offered ~ insurance * specialty + (1 | physician)"
                 )
  ),
  class = "mysterycall_logistic_model"
)

result <- mysterycall_interaction_table(fake_fit, "insurance", "specialty")
#> Warning: fit$model is NULL (likely a fake/stub object); LRT p-value set to NA.
print(result)
#> Interaction table: insurance x specialty  (conf_level = 0.95)
#> 
#> Stratum-specific odds ratios (OR with CI):
#>                            term   or ci_lower ci_upper p-value
#>  insuranceMedicaid:specialtyGYN 0.64     0.42     0.97   0.032
#>   insuranceMedicaid:specialtyOB 1.36     0.94     1.97   0.103
#> 
#> Omnibus LRT p-value: NA
#> 
#> The interaction between insurance and specialty was undetermined (LRT could not be computed) (LRT p=NA).
